articles.title: The Salesman in the Oval Office
articles.summary: On June 24, NATO's Secretary General presented a significant "sales pitch" in the Oval Office, utilizing charts and presentation boards. Mark Rutte was prominently involved in this high-level briefing. This interaction likely focused on crucial strategic proposals or resource allocations pertinent to the alliance's future, indicating an important diplomatic engagement on defence matters.

articles.title: 39k-Mile 2009 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 2LZ
articles.summary: This article details a highly modified 2009 Chevrolet Corvette Z06, focusing on its extensively upgraded 7.0-liter LS7 V8 engine. Key enhancements include an AHP camshaft, ported cylinder heads, and revised valvetrain components, significantly boosting its performance. Aspirants can note the practical application of automotive engineering principles in performance tuning and vehicle modification.

articles.title: U.S. Navy Aircraft Carrier Hosted International Helicopter Exchange
articles.summary: The U.S. Navy's Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN 71) has arrived at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii. Its deployment is specifically for participating in Exercise Rim of the Pacific (RIMPAC) 2026, a major multinational maritime exercise. This arrival signifies preparations for one of the world's largest naval drills, involving various nations to enhance interoperability and strengthen partnerships.

articles.title: My Lord and My God: The Living Faith of St. Thomas
articles.summary: Each year on July 3rd, Christians globally, particularly in India, observe a significant commemoration for St. Thomas the Apostle. This annual remembrance goes beyond a mere liturgical calendar date, serving as a profound moment for reflection and honouring his enduring legacy. The article underscores St. Thomas's deep historical and spiritual connection to the Christian community, especially highlighting his importance within the Indian context.

articles.title: Russia waged a drone campaign in Europe and likely launched drones from shadow ships, report says
articles.summary: A report suggests Russia used "shadow ships" to covertly launch drones over Europe, causing repeated disruptions to civilian aviation. These drones reportedly monitored military sites and tested the air defenses of NATO nations. This tactic highlights Russia's use of unconventional methods for intelligence gathering and probing adversaries' readiness, raising significant security concerns for European stability and international relations, particularly for SSB aspirants studying hybrid warfare.
